vocabulary.meaning_en: sad or worried because something bad happened
a situation when people do not have the same opinion
vocabulary.example: We had a small disagreement about the plan.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an angry talk between people who disagree
vocabulary.example: The two brothers had an argument.
In my opinion, the test was easy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a way of thinking about something
vocabulary.example: Try to see it from my perspective.

vocabulary.meaning_en: annoyed because you cannot do or change something
vocabulary.example: I felt frustrated when the computer stopped working.

vocabulary.meaning_en: feelings like anger, sadness or happiness
vocabulary.example: It's normal to have strong emotions.

vocabulary.note_ar: give someone space = اتركه وحده قليلًا
vocabulary.note_en: give someone space = leave them alone for a while

vocabulary.example: Let's wait a little and cool off.

vocabulary.meaning_en: succeed in dealing with a problem
vocabulary.example: We can overcome this problem together.
Don't let one bad day ruin your week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an idea about what someone should do
vocabulary.note_ar: غير معدودة: some advice (لا نقول an advice)
vocabulary.example: My teacher gave me good advice.

fine_lines.title: disagreement vs argument
fine_lines.explanation_ar: disagreement اختلاف في الرأي وقد يكون هادئًا. argument جدال فيه غضب وأصوات مرتفعة غالبًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A disagreement is having different opinions. An argument is an angry talk.

examples.sentence: We had a disagreement, but we stayed calm.
They had an argument and shouted.

fine_lines.title: calm down vs cool off
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلاهما بمعنى يهدأ. calm down عامة (من الغضب أو الخوف أو القلق)، و cool off تُستخدم غالبًا بعد الغضب أو الشجار.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean become calm. "Cool off" is usually used after anger or an argument.

examples.sentence: Give him an hour to cool off.

expressions.meaning_en: Ask if someone has a problem.
expressions.example: You look tired. Are you okay?

expressions.meaning_en: Say what you notice about someone's feelings.
Say this when someone tells you bad news.
expressions.example: My cat is sick. I'm sorry to hear that.

expressions.phrase: Do you want to talk about it?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل تريد أن تتحدث عن الأمر؟
expressions.meaning_en: Offer to listen to someone's problem.
expressions.example: You look sad. Do you want to talk about it?

expressions.meaning_en: Thank someone for caring about you.
expressions.example: Thanks for asking. I appreciate your concern.

expressions.meaning_en: Talk about a problem until you solve it.
expressions.example: Let's sit down and talk it out.
Take your time. I can wait.

expressions.meaning_en: Thank someone who listened to your problem.
expressions.example: Thank you for listening. I feel better now.

expressions.phrase: Friends are here to help each other.
expressions.example: Don't worry. Friends are here to help each other.

grammar.title: Describing feelings: look / feel + adjective
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد look (يبدو) و feel (يشعر) نستخدم صفة وليس ظرفًا: You look upset. I feel frustrated.
grammar.explanation_en: After look and feel use an adjective: You look upset. I feel better.

grammar.title: Past simple: telling what happened
grammar.explanation_ar: لنحكي ما حدث نستخدم الماضي البسيط. أفعال شاذة في الدرس: have → had، say → said، get → got، go → went. والنفي: didn't + الفعل في أصله.
grammar.explanation_en: To tell what happened, use the past simple. Irregular verbs here: had, said, got, went. Negative: didn't + base verb.
examples: I had a disagreement with my friend.
We said things we didn't mean.

grammar.title: Giving advice: "Have you thought about...?" / "It's important to..."
grammar.explanation_ar: لتقديم نصيحة بلطف: Have you thought about + فعل ing؟ أو It's important to + الفعل.
grammar.explanation_en: To give advice politely: Have you thought about + verb-ing? / It's important to + verb.
examples: Have you thought about giving it some time?
Have you thought about calling her?

questions.question: Your friend looks sad. What do you say?
questions.explanation_ar: نسأل Are you okay? عندما يبدو الشخص حزينًا.
questions.explanation_en: We ask "Are you okay?" when someone looks sad.

questions.question: My friend is sick. — I'm sorry ___ that.
questions.explanation_ar: العبارة الصحيحة: I'm sorry to hear that.
questions.explanation_en: The phrase is "I'm sorry to hear that".

questions.question: What is an "argument"?
questions.explanation_en: An argument is an angry talk.

questions.question: We both got ___ and said things we didn't mean.
questions.explanation_en: We need a feeling adjective: frustrated.

questions.question: "Take your time" means...
questions.explanation_ar: Take your time تعني لا تستعجل.

questions.question: Have you thought about ___ it some time?
questions.explanation_ar: بعد about نستخدم الفعل مع ing.

questions.question: I value our friendship. "Value" here means...
questions.explanation_ar: value هنا تعني يقدّر ويعتبره مهمًا جدًا.
questions.explanation_en: Value means think it is very important.

questions.question: Thank you for listening! — ___
questions.explanation_en: "Anytime" is a friendly reply to thanks.

questions.question: It's important to give your friend some space to ___.
questions.explanation_ar: cool off تعني يهدأ بعد الغضب.
questions.explanation_en: Cool off means become calm after anger.
